title: When the new wiring goes in: all at once, or one circuit at a time?
ask: When the new harness is installed, after the design is frozen, do you move every circuit over in one stretch, or keep the car starting on its old wiring while circuits move one at a time?
why: Your answer to block 00.29 was: "car currently does not start, broke down no wireing changes have been made". Understood. The breakdown is recorded as a car issue (K-025). This question is not about the car today. It is about install steps E26 to E28, months from now, after the design is frozen and the parts are bought. At E26 the key and the column switches (lights, turn, wipers, hazard) are rewired as signals into the new PMU, and from then on they cannot also run the old wiring. The install plan assumes the old wiring still starts the car through those weeks, and it cannot. The interior is out for the whole build (D-387), so the car is not driven during the install either way. The only question is whether it should still start.
options:
(a) All at once. Plug in the new column wiring and move every circuit over in one stretch (E26 to E28 back to back), using the migration table as the test order. Nothing extra to buy. The car does not start until the last circuit has moved, and a fault found late is found with everything already moved.
(b) Lights and motors first, switches last. The old key and switches keep running the old wiring while each light and motor moves over one at a time. Each moved circuit is tested from a temporary box of toggle switches (about 30 dollars), and the real switches move last. The car keeps starting on its old wiring until that last step.
recommend: (a), unless you want the car to keep starting on its old wiring through the install weeks. It has fewer temporary wires to get wrong and costs nothing.
stops: The wording of install steps E26 to E28 and the migration table (R1). Nothing already bought changes.
